newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - November 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - November 27.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Wednesday.
- The British government and Sinn Fein were locked in a war of words last night as hopes receded for a new IRA ceasefire.
- The blockade of French ports and roads by French truckers is costing Irish exporters more than three million Irish pounds a day in lost sales.
- Irish President Mary Robinson has rejected claims by Ulster Unionist Party leader David Trimble that she failed to adhere to proper protocol on her visits to Northern Ireland.
- The Irish Prime Minister, John Bruton has repeated that Ireland will "definitely" be a member of the EMU.
- The board of Aer Lingus will meet on Thursday to consider a new five-year plan for the future of the airline.
- The country's largest nursing union demanded a new salary deal that woulds cost the government another 40 million Irish pounds.
- Intense behind-the-scenes talks are keeping alive the prospect of a new IRA ceasefire.
- Fears were growing last night of a stiff petrol price rise in Ireland's January budget following Britain's 13p-per-gallon increase on Tuesday.
- A judge on Tuesday criticised the police after eight officers turned up in a court to prosecute a 10-year-old boy.
- The government is considering a crackdown on those who stay on the dole after refusing job offers.
